comment: #627 docs gallery (L2): the lighting sections of scripts/lighting/gallery.py, which also renders the exposure section from lighting_624.json and the materials section from lighting_615_gallery.json. The composition is the prototype's (scripts/studio_lights/placement.py, shadows.py and atmosphere.py on proto/studio-lights): 1rx1 at 960x540, inorganic removed, a grey90 surface on m and polymer with the NADPH as sticks (util.cbay), depth_cue 0, metal_shadows 1, async_builds 0, metal_light_air_time pinned at 2.0 s, the harness's L1 view turned y -25 (no orient), on the harness's black background; rt0 unless the tag ends in _rt1. Every lit scene builds its rig with the real commands (cmd.lights, cmd.atmosphere) inside cmd._lg_rig, a function the cmd.set_lights wrapper calls instead of installing the harness's rig: the frozen harness calls cmd.set_lights after the scene's lines, then asserts the rig is on. The wrapper is installed once per process (hasattr guard: the app runs each script twice); lights and atmosphere never call cmd.set_lights, so it cannot recurse. Python calls, not cmd.do, so a bad argument raises and the image fails. Sections, by tag prefix: rig_ (PyMOL's own lights, then each preset in presets() order), light_ (one field at a time on the prototype's sweep spot: beam, softness, warmth, colour with a coloured rim), place_ (target=, highlight= and rim=, a camera light vs a pinned one after the molecule turns), shadow_ (the prototype's red/blue pair: none, red, both, four lights with three shadowed, both traced), air_ (haze, dust, rt0 vs rt1, backlit, crossing beams, and the dust at metal_light_air_time 0, 1 and 2). place_highlight and place_highlight_rim use highlight=m and polymer and resi 124 (His124), picked headless: its centroid projects within 0.1 of the view centre at any window aspect (the off-screen test uses the live aspect) and the pick through it lands on its own atoms (0.13 A outside CG's vdW sphere); the NADPH was refused because the pick through its centroid hits Gly43's surface in front of it. highlight= needs a sized viewport, and the app runs PYMOL_AUTOCMD's first pass at launch, before the window has one (get_viewport 0x1: 'the viewport has no size'); that pass adds a dark key instead (_lg_sized, intensity 0), and the pass before the export, the one the image shows, places the light with highlight=. Were the export pass ever unsized, both place_highlight images would be the same dark key, which the gallery's rim check and the eye catch. gallery.py's SECTIONS lists each section's order, captions and difference checks; testing/tests/raymol/lighting_gallery.py runs every scene in-process.
